page.layout: One page of running text in a single column; no margin notes, no notes below the text. Running head at top centre: EPISTOLA.

main_text.p: hos quoq̃ promtè & libêter secuturos, meliusq̃ res humanas esse habituras. Noti sunt elegantes hi uersus Claudiani, de institutione Principis:
main_text.l: Tu ciuem patremq̃ geras, tu consule cunctis.
In commune iubes si quid, censesq̃ tenendum,
Primus iussa subi: tunc obseruantior æqui
Fit populus, nec ferre uetat, cum uiderit ipsum
Regis ad exemplum: nec sic inflectere sensus
Humanos edicta ualent, quàm uita regentis.
Mobile mutatur semper cum Principe uulgus.
main_text.p: Idem Historicus laudans Antoninum Philosophum Imperatorem, hac de eo memoria mandauit: Ὅτι μὲν ἐκ πάντων ...

page.notes: Greek sentence (Ὅτι μὲν ἐκ παίδων ... ἐν δὲ ἑνὶ ἡλικίῳ, ἵνα ... ἀληθῶς ἀγαθὸς ἀνὴρ ἦν, καὶ ἐδὲ ... ἐπιεικέστατος εἶχε) is only partly legible in the scan; the Greek shown above is an approximation and should be checked against the page. Several lines of Greek near the end of the paragraph are not reliably readable and are marked here rather than guessed. The paragraph ends in mid-line "Vtinā uerò Principes uiri, & omnes alij, qui eis proximos dignitatis ciuilis gradus obtinent, reuera boni esse studeant, sibiq̃ similes sint maneantq̃: nec locum dent uanitati & leuitati desultoriæ, quæ ferè ingentem ruinam secum trahit. Vidimus nostro seculo Regem, qui cum nec Euangelij lucem, qua illustratum erat cor eius, eo quo debebat loco haberet, nec personam sibi de-" and continues at the foot of the page with the word "bi de-" — the page ends mid-sentence, and the lower part of the page is not transcribed.
